questions.question: A sample of 40 fourth-grade students was selected at random from a certain school. The 40 students completed a survey about the morning announcements, and 32 thought the announcements were helpful. Which of the following is the largest population to which the results of the survey can be applied?
options: The 40 students who were surveyed
All fourth-grade students at the school
All students at the school
All fourth-grade students in the county in which the school is located

questions.question: A polling agency recently surveyed 1,000 adults who were selected at random from a large city and asked each of the adults, "Are you satisfied with the quality of air in the city?" Of those surveyed, 78 percent responded that they were satisfied with the quality of air in the city. Based on the results of the survey, which of the following statements must be true? 1. Of all adults in the city, 78 percent are satisfied with the quality of air in the city. 2. If another 1,000 adults selected at random from the city were surveyed, 78 percent of them would report they are satisfied with the quality of air in the city. 3. If 1,000 adults selected at random from a different city were surveyed, 78 percent of them would report they are satisfied with the quality of air in the city.
options: None
Il only
I and II only
I and III only

The table displays the information for the 40 teams in the sample that practiced for at least 3 hours per week. Number of points per round Hours practiced 6 to 13 points 14 or more points Total 3 to 5 hours 6 4 10 More than 5 hours 4 26 30 Total 10 30 40 Which of the following is the largest population to which the results of the study can be generalized?

The 55 trivia teams in the sample
The 40 trivia teams in the sample that practiced for at least 3 hours per week
All trivia teams in the tournament

questions.question: A market researcher selected 200 people at random from a group of people who indicated that they liked a certain book. The 200 people were shown a movie based on the book and then asked whether they liked or disliked the movie. Of those surveyed, 95% said they disliked the movie. Which of the following inferences can appropriately be drawn from this survey result?
options: At least 95% of people who go see movies will dislike this movie.
At least 95% of people who read books will dislike this movie.
Most people who dislike this book will like this movie.
Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.

questions.question: A school estimates student satisfaction by surveying 30 students who attend the optional celebration. What is the main concern?
options: Random assignment bias
Selection bias, because attendees may be more satisfied than other students
The sample is too representative
The survey necessarily proves causation
questions.explanation: B is correct. The sampling location systematically favors a subgroup likely to differ in satisfaction.
questions.teachingTopic: 识别偏差、混杂变量和过度推断

questions.question: In a study of 35 neighborhoods, areas with more bike lanes also have newer buildings and lower traffic noise. The study attributes the outcome entirely to bike lanes. What is a key concern?
options: The study used too many measurements.
Bike lanes cannot be associated with the outcome.
Related neighborhood differences may be confounding variables.
A correlation automatically rules out confounding.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Other neighborhood characteristics related to both the explanatory feature and the outcome can confound the association.
questions.teachingTopic: 识别偏差、混杂变量和过度推断

questions.question: A survey of 40 members of one garden club finds that most prefer native plants. The report concludes that all homeowners share that preference. What is wrong with the conclusion?
options: It uses a sample rather than a census, which is always invalid.
It reports a preference rather than a numerical value.
It fails to impose a treatment even though the goal is only to describe a preference.
It overgeneralizes from a narrow, unrepresentative sample.
questions.explanation: D is correct. A narrow convenience group is not a representative basis for a much broader population claim.
questions.teachingTopic: 识别偏差、混杂变量和过度推断
